title: Uniqueness of vague limits: two measures on ℝ^P that are finite on compact sets and give equal integrals to every continuous compactly supported function are equal (parent fact (F6), step 5b)
statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let ν₁, ν₂ be measures on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra) such that ν₁(K) ≠ ∞ and ν₂(K) ≠ ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, and ∫ f dν₁ = ∫ f dν₂ for every continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support. Then ν₁ = ν₂.
lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (ν₁ ν₂ : Measure (Euclid P)), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ν₁ K ≠ ∞) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ν₂ K ≠ ∞) → (∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → ∫ x, f x ∂ν₁ = ∫ x, f x ∂ν₂) → ν₁ = ν₂
